## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

## Agent details

Written with Claude Code: the analysis, measurements and test plan below.

**TLDR:** At generator DP>1, linear-attention models (GDN, KDA layers) now keep FULL CUDA graphs instead of falling back to FULL_DECODE_ONLY, so prefill and mixed steps replay a graph instead of running eager. Qwen3.5-35B-A3B at DP 2 x EP 2 (GB300): one prefill 0.68 s -> 39-157 ms (2k-16k tokens); at EP = DP = 4, output tokens per second 1.55x / 2.02x at 64 / 256 sequences per engine (earlier measurement). No recipe runs this today: the one hybrid DP>1 recipe uses eager mode because its MoE dispatcher can't be captured; once it moves to Dist-MoE, this PR lets it run FULL instead of FULL_DECODE_ONLY.

```text
one step at DP = 2: rank 0 prefills a 16k-token chunk, rank 1 decodes 24 sequences
main:     linear attention reports uniform-only at DP>1 -> mode FULL_DECODE_ONLY -> both ranks eager
this PR:  full support -> mode FULL -> both ranks replay the 16384-token mixed graph (rank 1 padded to it)
```

```python
# TorchTitanLinearAttentionMetadataBuilder.get_cudagraph_support
# before
if parallel.data_parallel_size != 1 or parallel.use_ubatching or parallel.enable_dbo:
    return AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH
# after
if (parallel.data_parallel_size != 1 and is_in_batch_invariant_mode()) or parallel.use_ubatching or parallel.enable_dbo:
    return AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH
```

**Stack** (4 PRs, merge 1 -> 4; this PR is in **bold**)

| # | PR | Independent? | Needs (stack positions) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #5704 vLLM generator: decode-specialized FULL graphs for every model, DP>1-safe | yes | — |
| **2** | **#5490 FULL CUDA graphs for linear-attention generators at DP>1** | **no** | **1** |
| 3 | #5489 vLLM generator: 128-token KV pages when FA4 runs attention | yes | — |
| 4 | #5706 Muse Spark: use varlen attention in the CP-16 LoRA SFT recipe | yes | — |

**Problem**
1. At DP>1, the linear-attention metadata builder tells vLLM it can only graph uniform (decode-only) batches, so vLLM turns FULL into FULL_DECODE_ONLY.
2. FULL_DECODE_ONLY has no graph for a step with prefill tokens, so that step runs eager.
3. vLLM runs every DP rank in the same graph mode, so when one rank prefills, the other ranks' decodes run eager too.
4. **Who hits it:** the generator allows DP>1 only to supply EP ranks (`Generator.Config.__post_init__`), so any EP generator of a hybrid model in FULL mode. Today that is no recipe: `rl_grpo_qwen35_35b_a3b_terminal_bench` (generator DP 2 x EP 4) runs `mode="NONE"` because its all-to-all MoE dispatcher copies split sizes to the host, which graph capture rejects (`torchtitan_recipes/rl/verifiers_terminal_bench.py:299-306, 413`).
5. **Cost:** an eager prefill takes ~0.68 s at any size from 2k to 16k tokens (flat, so host-bound), vs 39-157 ms replayed (Results).

**Solution**
1. The builder reports full CUDA-graph support at DP>1. Micro-batching and dual-batch overlap still report uniform-only.
2. Padded decode ranks need no new code: position 1's dispatcher already replays the mixed graph for a decode batch above the largest decode graph.
3. **Batch-invariant runs keep uniform-only support at DP>1 (TODO):** the packed kernels with cached state don't match the decode kernels bitwise (measured for GDN; KDA assumed).
4. Unchanged: DP = 1, FULL_DECODE_ONLY and NONE modes, ubatching / DBO, the decode graphs, every recipe.

**Results**
```text
Numerics: not bitwise at DP>1 on steps where any rank prefills (eager -> graph padded to the next capture size). All-decode
steps are unchanged (same decode graphs); a decoding rank switches to the packed kernels only when a peer's padded batch is
larger than the largest decode graph (256 tokens here).
  every rank, own 1991-token prefill:   eager -> 2048-token graph          mean |dlogprob| 7.3e-3 (max 0.16), 0 of 24 flip
  decoding rank, also padded to 16384:  decode kernels -> packed kernels   1.6e-2 before the first flip (max 0.16), 2 of 24 flip
  the 2 flips are near-ties, top-token logprob before / after: -1.88 / -1.85 (request 3, token 7), -1.60 / -1.65 (request 21, token 4)
  yardstick: mean |trainer - generator| logprob 1.690e-2 main | 1.629e-2 this PR (earlier measurement, below)
```
```text
GB300, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base, DP 2 x EP 2 Dist-MoE, FULL, max_num_batched_tokens 16384, max_num_seqs 256 (caps decode).
Same script, back to back, same engine settings; "before" = position 1 (main's behavior for linear attention at DP>1).
prefill, one prompt, add -> finished (2 engine steps), ms     before   after
  2048 tokens                                                  686.8    39.3   -94%
  4096 tokens                                                  685.9    55.7   -92%
  8192 tokens                                                  684.4    88.9   -87%
  16384 tokens                                                 682.6   156.8   -77%
decode step, ms (512-token context)    bs1    8.44 ->  8.44
                                       bs4    8.79 ->  8.79
                                       bs16   9.31 ->  9.31
                                       bs64  10.55 -> 10.61
                                       bs256 17.63 -> 17.65
step where rank 0 prefills 16000 tokens and rank 1 decodes 24:
  before: both ranks eager (NONE)      after: both ranks replay the 16384-token mixed graph
cost per rank: graph capture 9 graphs, 32 s, 0.12 GiB -> 24 graphs, 71 s, 1.80 GiB; KV cache 125.91 -> 124.29 GiB
```

Earlier measurement (this PR's first version, main plus the Dist-MoE inference PRs, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base, 4 engines, EP = DP = 4, GSM8K prompts, 256 output tokens). The first version = this PR + position 1's dispatcher change. For linear attention at DP>1, position 1 alone changes nothing (the mode stays FULL_DECODE_ONLY and the dispatcher acts only in FULL), so this compares the same two behaviors:
```text
                                     seq/engine   main        this PR
output tok/s, 4 engines                  64      10.4k   ->  16.2k    1.55x
                                         256     16.2k   ->  32.7k    2.02x
mean |trainer - generator| logprob      256      1.690e-2 -> 1.629e-2  (trainer: Dist-MoE EP 4 + FSDP 4)
```
- Training: not touched (generator only).

You may ask: why a batch-invariant clause here when position 1 has one? Position 1's acts only when eager is allowed. At DP>1, after the ranks sync, vLLM allows only FULL, so a padded batch-invariant decode rank would run the packed kernels without any error.

NOTE: Not run: KDA at DP>1 (no recipe), batch-invariant mode end to end, a full RL job.

**Follow up**
- [ ] Migrate `rl_grpo_qwen35_35b_a3b_terminal_bench` to Dist-MoE, then FULL graphs.
- [ ] Batch-invariant GDN/KDA: make the packed kernels with cached state match the decode kernels bitwise, then drop both batch-invariant clauses (the TODO in `linear_attention.py`).

**Test plan**
```bash
pytest tests/rl/unit_tests/gpu/test_gdn_graph_metadata.py -k dp_support_level   # 3 cases; needs no GPU, but lives in gpu/, so CI runs it in the GPU job
torchrun --nproc-per-node=2 -m pytest tests/rl/unit_tests/gpu/test_generator_dp_cudagraph.py::test_vllm_dp_linear_attention_full_graphs   # new: 1 passed (GB300, 57 s); in CI's H100 RL job (needs SM90+)
pytest tests/rl/unit_tests/cpu      # stack head: 510 passed, 9 skipped, 3 failed; the same 3 fail on main in this env
# DP = 1 regression checks on the stack head's previous revision (positions 1-3; since then comment- and test-only changes + rebase), GB300
pytest tests/rl/unit_tests/gpu/test_gdn_cudagraph.py tests/rl/unit_tests/gpu/test_gdn_graph_metadata.py   # 12 passed (Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base)
torchrun --nproc-per-node=2 -m pytest tests/rl/unit_tests/gpu/test_bitwise_parity.py::TestBitwiseParityQwen35DebugVarlen   # 4 passed
```
- New GPU test `test_vllm_dp_linear_attention_full_graphs`: Qwen3.5 MoE debug model, DP = world size, FULL graphs. Rank 0 prefills a 1500-token prompt; on every rank that step replays a FULL mixed graph of at least 1500 tokens: rank 0's prefill (eager before this PR), a decoding rank padded to it, and an idle rank's dummy batch padded to it.
- The DP = 2 numbers above: a 2-GPU script that builds TorchTitan's `VLLMEngine` for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base with Dist-MoE and records every step's dispatch.

nodes.body:
**Claude finished @felipemello1's task in 2m 18s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/40956497009)

---
**Approve** -- [review](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5490#pullrequestreview) posted. One optional item: trimming the unit test.

**Verdict: Approve.** The PR relaxes one condition that position 1's dispatcher made unnecessary, it is well measured, and the remaining item is optional test trimming.

**What this PR does.** At DP>1, `TorchTitanLinearAttentionMetadataBuilder.get_cudagraph_support` now reports `ALWAYS` instead of `UNIFORM_BATCH`, so vLLM keeps FULL mode for GDN/KDA models and no longer downgrades to FULL_DECODE_ONLY. Steps that contain prefill tokens on any DP rank now replay a mixed graph instead of running eager. Batch-invariant mode, ubatching and DBO still report uniform-only. DP>1 now behaves the same as DP=1, where FULL already captures mixed graphs, and position 1's dispatcher already sends DP-padded decode batches to the mixed graph.

**Example.**
```text
Qwen3.5 MoE, DP=2, cuda_graph.mode="FULL"
step: rank 0 prefills a 1500-token chunk, rank 1 decodes 3 seqs (or is idle)
base (pos. 1): UNIFORM_BATCH -> resolved mode FULL_DECODE_ONLY -> both ranks NONE (eager)
this PR:       ALWAYS        -> mode FULL -> both ranks replay the >=1500-token mixed graph
               (rank 1 padded; an idle rank's dummy batch also padded)
batch_invariant=True at DP=2: unchanged (FULL_DECODE_ONLY), so bitwise parity is kept
```

### Should consider
- `tests/rl/unit_tests/gpu/test_gdn_graph_metadata.py:73` -- the parametrized test mostly restates the boolean. Keep only the `(DP=2, batch_invariant) -> UNIFORM_BATCH` case, which nothing else guards (inline).

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- **Gate.** The problem is real on the base branch: the eager prefill is host-bound at about 0.68 s. The fix is in the layer that owns it: the builder's support level was the only thing forcing FULL_DECODE_ONLY, and the reason for it (padded decode ranks) is now handled by `TorchTitanCudagraphDispatcher.dispatch`. No recipe uses this today. The consumer is named (`rl_grpo_qwen35_35b_a3b_terminal_bench` after it moves to Dist-MoE), and the change removes a restriction rather than adding a knob, so it passes.
- **Batch-invariant ordering.** `get_cudagraph_support` reads a process-global flag. `Generator.__init__` calls `set_batch_invariance` (`generator.py:217`) before it builds the engine, and the engine uses `external_launcher`, so vLLM's workers run in the same process and see the flag when the cudagraph mode is resolved.
- **Two batch-invariant clauses.** When batch-invariant mode is on at DP>1, the mode resolves to FULL_DECODE_ONLY, so the dispatcher clause in `worker.py:83` (FULL only) never runs there. It still matters at DP=1. The TODO that refers to both clauses is accurate.
- **CI split.** Giving each test its own torchrun launch follows the file's rule that each engine frees its GPU memory only at process exit.
- **New GPU test.** It fails on the base branch (no FULL non-uniform record), so it guards this change. It also covers the idle-rank dummy batch through the packed path, which no other test covers.
- **Cost.** Per rank, about 1.7 GiB more graph memory and about 40 s more capture time at max_num_batched_tokens 16384. This is the same cost DP=1 FULL already pays, and it is documented.

</details>

Not verified: KDA at DP>1, including the idle rank's dummy batch going through the KDA packed path in a mixed graph. This needs a GPU run, and no test or recipe covers it.

Two of these three cases mostly restate the condition. `(2, False, ALWAYS)` is already covered end to end by `test_vllm_dp_linear_attention_full_graphs`: on the base branch that test gets FULL_DECODE_ONLY and its assertion fails. `(1, True, ALWAYS)` checks behavior this PR doesn't change. The case nothing else covers is `(2, True, UNIFORM_BATCH)`. That is the bitwise-parity guard, and if it broke it would fail silently, because no batch-invariant hybrid test runs at DP>1. I suggest keeping only that case, as a plain test named for the invariant (e.g. `test_batch_invariant_dp_keeps_uniform_only`). Separately, the PR says this runs on CPU, but it lives in `gpu/`, so it only runs in the GPU job. That's fine, just be aware of it.

reviews.body:
**Verdict: Approve.** The PR relaxes one condition that position 1's dispatcher made unnecessary, it is well measured, and the remaining item is optional test trimming.

**What this PR does.** At DP>1, `TorchTitanLinearAttentionMetadataBuilder.get_cudagraph_support` now reports `ALWAYS` instead of `UNIFORM_BATCH`, so vLLM keeps FULL mode for GDN/KDA models and no longer downgrades to FULL_DECODE_ONLY. Steps that contain prefill tokens on any DP rank now replay a mixed graph instead of running eager. Batch-invariant mode, ubatching and DBO still report uniform-only. DP>1 now behaves the same as DP=1, where FULL already captures mixed graphs, and position 1's dispatcher already sends DP-padded decode batches to the mixed graph.

**Example.**
```text
Qwen3.5 MoE, DP=2, cuda_graph.mode="FULL"
step: rank 0 prefills a 1500-token chunk, rank 1 decodes 3 seqs (or is idle)
base (pos. 1): UNIFORM_BATCH -> resolved mode FULL_DECODE_ONLY -> both ranks NONE (eager)
this PR:       ALWAYS        -> mode FULL -> both ranks replay the >=1500-token mixed graph
               (rank 1 padded; an idle rank's dummy batch also padded)
batch_invariant=True at DP=2: unchanged (FULL_DECODE_ONLY), so bitwise parity is kept
```

### Should consider
- `tests/rl/unit_tests/gpu/test_gdn_graph_metadata.py:73` -- the parametrized test mostly restates the boolean. Keep only the `(DP=2, batch_invariant) -> UNIFORM_BATCH` case, which nothing else guards (inline).

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- **Gate.** The problem is real on the base branch: the eager prefill is host-bound at about 0.68 s. The fix is in the layer that owns it: the builder's support level was the only thing forcing FULL_DECODE_ONLY, and the reason for it (padded decode ranks) is now handled by `TorchTitanCudagraphDispatcher.dispatch`. No recipe uses this today. The consumer is named (`rl_grpo_qwen35_35b_a3b_terminal_bench` after it moves to Dist-MoE), and the change removes a restriction rather than adding a knob, so it passes.
- **Batch-invariant ordering.** `get_cudagraph_support` reads a process-global flag. `Generator.__init__` calls `set_batch_invariance` (`generator.py:217`) before it builds the engine, and the engine uses `external_launcher`, so vLLM's workers run in the same process and see the flag when the cudagraph mode is resolved.
- **Two batch-invariant clauses.** When batch-invariant mode is on at DP>1, the mode resolves to FULL_DECODE_ONLY, so the dispatcher clause in `worker.py:83` (FULL only) never runs there. It still matters at DP=1. The TODO that refers to both clauses is accurate.
- **CI split.** Giving each test its own torchrun launch follows the file's rule that each engine frees its GPU memory only at process exit.
- **New GPU test.** It fails on the base branch (no FULL non-uniform record), so it guards this change. It also covers the idle-rank dummy batch through the packed path, which no other test covers.
- **Cost.** Per rank, about 1.7 GiB more graph memory and about 40 s more capture time at max_num_batched_tokens 16384. This is the same cost DP=1 FULL already pays, and it is documented.

</details>

Not verified: KDA at DP>1, including the idle rank's dummy batch going through the KDA packed path in a mixed graph. This needs a GPU run, and no test or recipe covers it.
